title: Directions EMEA 2026, Day 2: Cowork, Agentic Development and Fabric
summary: Directions EMEA 2026 Day 2 covered AI orchestration across applications through Cowork, agentic AL development with BCQuality, native Business Central-Fabric integration, and platform performance improvements. The post explains how Business Central is evolving from individual Copilot features to broader multi-agent workflows with architectural implications for partners.
key_points: Cowork orchestrates business processes across Microsoft 365 and Business Central, with agents handling ERP operations while maintaining permissions and transaction integrity
AI-assisted AL development is shifting from code generation to managing development workflows, supported by BCQuality for Business Central-specific knowledge and BC-Bench for agent evaluation
Native Business Central-Fabric mirroring replicates ERP data without consuming Business Central APIs, but requires proper data modeling and security for analytics and agents
Platform improvements include table-extension storage optimization, AL-based index management, and Business Central Optimum collaboration for real-world performance
Partners face new architectural questions about multi-agent processes: ownership, approvals, failure handling, monitoring, and maintaining business rules enforcement across distributed workflows
versions: January 2027 (Customize with Copilot early access target)

quotes.text: Business Central must remain responsible for enforcing business rules, permissions, and transaction integrity, regardless of which agent initiates an operation.
quotes.why_it_matters: Establishes that multi-agent workflows don't reduce Business Central's core responsibility for data integrity and security, a critical architectural principle for distributed systems.

quotes.text: Generating code is becoming easier. Demonstrating that an agent can solve realistic Business Central development tasks correctly is a different challenge.
quotes.why_it_matters: Shows that AI-assisted development's real value lies not in code generation but in managing complete, validated development processes that meet real-world requirements.

quotes.text: Access to data is only part of the problem. Agents also need to understand what that data represents and how it should be interpreted.
quotes.why_it_matters: Highlights that data availability alone doesn't enable agent functionality; proper data semantics and modeling are essential for agents to make correct decisions.
